findings.issue: The original '../../lib/...' imports were one directory level too shallow (app/app/lib instead of app/lib), but the agent attributed the build failure to a Turbopack workspace-root quirk and never identified its own path-arithmetic error; it left behind a speculative note about a framework bug.
findings.suggestion: When a 'module not found' error appears for a path that demonstrably exists, resolve the path mechanically (e.g. `node -e "require.resolve(...)"` or realpath from the importing file) before hypothesizing about bundler internals; the resulting @/ alias is fine, but the root cause should have been named.

findings.issue: `pkill -f "next"` / `pkill -f "next-server"` matched the agent's own bash command string and killed its own shell three times, each time aborting a verification command (including one test run, turn 78).
findings.suggestion: Kill by port or PID (`fuser -k 3000/tcp`, `pgrep -f 'next-server' | xargs kill`) or use a pattern that can't match the invoking command; after the first occurrence this should never have recurred.

findings.issue: Two edit attempts to 'fix' an export that was already correct, based on a misreading of its own just-written file.
findings.suggestion: Grep/read the target text before editing when the previous write's content is uncertain.

findings.issue: Zero use of web search, docs, or the available skill/MCP guidance across the whole session, including while stuck for 8 turns on a suspected Turbopack behavior.
findings.suggestion: When a toolchain behaves contrary to expectation, spend one turn checking the official docs or release notes before building workarounds.

findings.issue: Removed loading="lazy" from card sprites so full-page screenshots would show all images; on pages with 256+ cards this loads every sprite eagerly for real users.
findings.suggestion: Keep lazy loading and instead scroll/force-load images before screenshotting (e.g. agent-browser eval scrolling or eager fetch), so the production tradeoff isn't driven by the verification tool.

summary: A well-run session: exhaustive up-front recon (spec, tests, fixtures, screenshots), a sound Next.js 16 architecture, and 54/54 acceptance tests passing on the first full run, followed by careful visual verification against the reference designs at both breakpoints and a green final suite after the last edit. The main blemishes are a build failure it misdiagnosed as a Turbopack quirk (its own relative-import depth was wrong; the alias workaround was fine but the cause was never named) and a pkill pattern that killed its own shell three times. Roughly 80 turns were used with perhaps 8-10 avoidable.
